And 2 Others on 16 October, 2025 Author: Ajit Kumar Bench: Ajit Kumar High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad Neutral Citation No. - 2025:Ahc:185812-Db High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad Writ - C No. - 33998 of 2025 Farzana .....Petitioner(s) Versus State Of U.P. And 2 Others .....Respondent(s) Counsel for Petitioner(s) : C.S.C. Farzana vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 16 October, 2025 2. By means of this petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution, petitioner has prayed for a writ of mandamus to command respondent No.- 3 to take decision upon the application of the petitioner moved for grant of license to open up buffalo meat shop. 3. It is contended by learned counsel for the petitioner that the said license is granted as per the provisions contained under the the regulations namely Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Business) Regulations, 2011.
texts.facts: 2. By means of this petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution, petitioner has prayed for a writ of mandamus to command respondent No.- 3 to take decision upon the application of the petitioner moved for grant of license to open up buffalo meat shop.
texts.arguments: 3. It is contended by learned counsel for the petitioner that the said license is granted as per the provisions contained under the the regulations namely Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Business) Regulations, 2011. It is further contended that under the relevant regulations no objection certificate has to be obtained either from the panchayat, municipality or corporation and the petitioner having obtained no objection certificate from the municipality, he is entitled to be granted license to run the meat shop. 4. Learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel states that since the matter is already engaging attention of the licensing authority, he may be directed to dispose of the pending claim of the petitioner as per the regulations referred to herein above.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 3. It is contended by learned counsel for the petitioner that the said license is granted as per the provisions contained under the the regulations namely Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Business) Regulations, 2011. It is further contended that under the relevant regulations no objection certificate has to be obtained either from the panchayat, municipality or corporation and the petitioner having obtained no objection certificate from the municipality, he is entitled to be granted license to run the meat shop. 4. Learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel states that since the matter is already engaging attention of the licensing authority, he may be directed to dispose of the pending claim of the petitioner as per the regulations referred to herein above.
